title: A low-cost continuous rumen simulation system for sustainable in vitro fermentation and feed evaluation in ruminant production
author: Kour, Malik, et al.
materials: To maintain optimal environmental conditions for rumen microbial growth, a precise temperature regulation system was installed in bioreactor. The temperature control unit involved integrating components such as thermostat sensors, heating and air circulation unit. These components were selected based on their reliability, accuracy, and compatibility with the bioreactor system. The unit was designed to simulate rumen temperature at 39±1 °C by continuously monitoring the bioreactor's internal temperature. Necessary adjustments were made to ensure consistent thermal conditions.

A temperature regulation unit was successfully developed to simulate the rumen environment by maintaining a stable temperature of 39±1 °C within the bioreactor. The unit was constructed using a thermostat sensor configured and calibrated to cutoff at 39.5 °C temperature with a wait time of 0.5 °C to avoid frequent switching. The heating unit was designed to switch on when the temperature fell below 39 °C and switch off at 39.5 °C, maintaining a consistent range [4]. The configured settings remain constant unless manually adjusted, eliminating the need for regular recalibration unless a temperature change is required. The dry-box heating method provided excellent temperature control within 0.5 °C. Flow rate calibration ensured consistent buffer supply, and cyclic motility pumps prevented sedimentation. This setup was suitable for further experimentation and application in simulating the rumen environment in vitro.

The Continuous Rumen Bioreactor (CRB) system consists of two modified fermentation vessels (16,36) housed in a thermostatically controlled incubator chamber (49). The system is designed to maintain conditions similar to the rumen environment, with continuous supply of artificial saliva, mixing, chyme removal, and gas collection.

The Rumen Simulation Technique (RUSITEC) is a well-established in vitro continuous fermentation system widely used for studying rumen function. While RUSITEC offers robust control over experimental variables, it has limitations in terms of cost, accessibility, and certain operational aspects. The developed CRB addresses several of these limitations while maintaining comparable functionality (Fig. 2B). steps.title: Select and modify vessels
steps.instruction: Choose two acrylic‑styrene vessels (1 L and 2.5 L). Drill and thread ports for continuous buffer inflow, chyme outflow, and gas‑tight fittings using O‑rings and Teflon tape. For the 1 L vessel, drill a hole 7 inches (≈17.8 cm) from the bottom (≈two‑thirds height) and thread it to serve as the chyme outlet with a capacity of 860 mL; fit a connector with O‑ring/Teflon tape. For the 2.5 L vessel, drill a hole 1 inch (≈2.5 cm) above the base for artificial saliva inlet via a T‑joint. Install a cap with a modular feed‑addition unit (removable cartridge with nylon bags).

steps.title: Install temperature regulation
steps.instruction: Mount a thermostat sensor, heating element and air‑circulation fan on the bioreactor. Calibrate the controller to cut off at 39.5 °C and to switch on when temperature falls below 39 °C, with a hysteresis of 0.5 °C, thereby maintaining 39 ± 1 °C inside the vessel. Use a dry‑box heating method for stable control.

steps.title: Prepare artificial saliva tank
steps.instruction: Use a 15 L polycarbonate container as the artificial saliva reservoir. Drill three holes in the cap: one for a CO₂ inlet pipe (for intermittent CO₂ flushing), one for an air‑safety valve (to prevent pressure buildup), and one for a USB port to power a submersible mixing pump. Fill the tank with artificial saliva prepared according to McDougall’s composition, keep it sterile and anaerobic, and run the submersible pump continuously to prevent salt settling.

steps.title: Assemble saliva delivery system
steps.instruction: Connect a peristaltic pump, three‑way valves and polyurethane tubing (8 mm, 6 mm or 9.5 mm as required) from the saliva tank to the bioreactor inlet. Attach a speed controller and timer module to the pump. Calibrate flow using the on/off timing table (Table 1): e.g., 10 s on/50 s off → 0.505 mL min⁻¹, 15 s on/50 s off → 0.831 mL min⁻¹, 20 s on/50 s off → 1.015 mL min⁻¹, etc. For experimental trials select a flow of 0.44 mL min⁻¹ for the 1 L vessel and 0.29 mL min⁻¹ for the 2.5 L vessel (matching the dilution rates of 0.40 mL min⁻¹ and 0.29 mL min⁻¹ used in preliminary tests).

substeps.instruction: Set the timer on‑time and off‑time according to the desired flow (see Table 1).
Verify the actual displaced volume by collecting the outflow for a known period.

steps.title: Install feed cartridge system
steps.instruction: For the 2.5 L vessel, drill a central 47 mm threaded hole in the cap and fit a lightweight PVC‑brass female adapter. Insert a feed cartridge consisting of a perforated PVC pipe, an end cap and a removable Teflon stopper through the adapter. Load nylon‑bagged or capsule‑contained substrate into the cartridge; the perforations allow exchange with rumen liquor. (The 1 L vessel originally used S‑shaped stainless‑steel hooks and nylon‑threaded capsules; retain this only if desired, noting limited mid‑experiment access.)

steps.title: Install motility pump and controller
steps.instruction: Connect a diaphragm pump (identified as the most suitable) to the bioreactor via plastic joints. Link the pump to a speed controller and a timer module set to simulate two rumen contractions per minute (intermittent mixing). Ensure the pump runs continuously throughout the trial, providing motility without blockage.

steps.title: Perform gas leak test
steps.instruction: Check the gas‑tight integrity of each vessel, its connectors and the gas‑collection assemblies before fermentation. Conduct a water‑immersion test followed by a pressure test using an air pump to confirm no leaks.

steps.title: Prepare inoculum and substrate
steps.instruction: Collect rumen liquor and fibrous material from freshly slaughtered goats. Transfer the contents to pre‑warmed (39 ± 1 °C) anaerobic containers, flush with CO₂ and keep at 39 °C during transport. Dry the substrate (concentrate + wheat‑straw roughage, 50:50) at 100 ± 2 °C for 24 h and grind finely. Weigh 2 g of the dried substrate for each trial.

steps.title: Load bioreactor and start operation
steps.instruction: For the 1 L vessel, add up to 500 mL of rumen liquor (max capacity 800 mL). For the 2.5 L vessel, add up to 1 L of rumen liquor (max capacity 2 L). Insert the feed cartridge with the 2 g substrate. Start the artificial saliva pump at the selected dilution rate (0.40 mL min⁻¹ for the 1 L vessel, 0.29 mL min⁻¹ for the 2.5 L vessel). Activate the diaphragm motility pump set to two contractions per minute. Verify temperature is maintained at 39 ± 1 °C.

steps.title: Monitor fermentation parameters
steps.instruction: Record pH, total gas production (mL g⁻¹ DM), methane production (mL g⁻¹ DM), motility score, protozoa count (×10⁴ mL⁻¹), and dry‑matter degradability (%) at regular intervals (e.g., days 1, 3, 5, 7 for the 1 L vessel; days 1, 10, 20, 30, 40 for the 2.5 L vessel).

steps.title: Collect gas in latex bladder
steps.instruction: Route gas from the vessel caps to latex gas bladders (selected as the optimal gas‑collection unit). Ensure the bladder is securely attached and monitor for any leakage.

steps.title: Clean and maintain system
steps.instruction: After each trial, disassemble the modular components (caps, feed cartridge, pumps, tubing). Rinse all parts with water, sterilize as needed, and re‑assemble for the next run. Verify that all O‑rings and Teflon tape seals are intact before reuse.
